experience.title: The Shift
experience.intro: A step-by-step journey shaping my product instinct through 4 milestones.

stage1.title: Problems Without a Sample Answer
stage1.lens: Math Major • Quang Trung High School for the Gifted
stage1.desc: Years in a specialized math program taught me to embrace difficult problems, start from first principles, and understand rather than memorize formulas.
stage1.takeaway: Always break a problem down to its most fundamental parts before solving it.

stage2.title: Mastering Code & Systems
stage2.desc: Long nights debugging capstone projects taught me that getting code to run is one thing — building a system that scales and stays maintainable is another.
stage2.takeaway: Deep technical understanding to know the limits of the tech and speak the same language as engineers.

stage3.title: When a Feature I Cared About Got Ignored
stage3.desc: Watching users drop off from a feature I spent a month coding taught me a hard lesson: no matter how polished the code, a product gets abandoned if it solves the wrong need.
stage3.takeaway: The mindset shift: don't just ask "how do I build this," always ask "why would anyone use this?"

stage4.title: Owning Products End-to-End
stage4.desc: I combine mathematical thinking, technical depth, and AI to take a product from idea to user experience — and take full ownership along the way.
stage4.takeaway: Turning complex technology into simple digital experiences that create real value.

toolbox.title: Supporting Skills
toolbox.intro: Other hands-on skills proven through real products and real work.

ga4.title: Conversion Funnel Analysis & Anomaly Detection
ga4.description: Traced the cross-channel purchase journey, spotted the Mobile checkout bottleneck, and filtered out ~40k bot sessions to keep the data clean.
ga4.takeaway: Optimization recommendations grounded in real user behavior, not guesswork.

powerbi.title: Data Visualization & Product Mix Analysis
powerbi.description: Used SQL to mine raw data and built a Power BI dashboard to reveal revenue and performance across product lines.
powerbi.takeaway: Recommended scaling the Standard line and cutting the underperforming Tourist line — a data-driven call, not a gut call.

prd.title: PRD, User Stories & Use Case Specs
prd.description: Turned user problems into clear PRDs and User Stories with acceptance criteria, bridging Business and Engineering.
prd.takeaway: Made sure both sides shared the same logic before a single line of code was written.

sql.title: Data Querying & Business Performance Breakdown
sql.description: Wrote multi-table SQL queries to measure revenue and operational KPIs per branch.
sql.takeaway: Ran the analysis independently, without waiting on a data team.

erd.title: Business Logic & Database Modeling
erd.description: Designed the E-ERD and automation rules (loyalty points, promotions, inventory) to keep the system consistent.
erd.takeaway: Spoke the same language as Backend and Solution Architects from day one.
